title: Weak-equivalence comparisons for cofibrant colimit constructions
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category in the sense of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], with all small limits and colimits; smallness is relative to fixed universes, which may be enlarged. The following colimit comparison assertions hold.

(a) A small coproduct of weak equivalences between cofibrant objects is a weak equivalence, and these coproducts are cofibrant.

(b) Given a map of spans $(X\leftarrow A\xrightarrow{i}B)\to(X'\leftarrow A'\xrightarrow{i'}B')$, assume all six objects are cofibrant, $i,i'$ are cofibrations, and the three component maps are weak equivalences. Then the induced map $X\amalg_A B\to X'\amalg_{A'}B'$ is a weak equivalence, and both pushouts are cofibrant.

(c) Let $\theta$ be a small nonzero limit ordinal. Let $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ and $(Y_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ be ordinal-indexed diagrams with cofibrant initial objects, cofibration successor maps, and colimit cocones at every nonzero limit ordinal less than $\theta$. Every natural transformation $u_\alpha:X_\alpha\to Y_\alpha$ whose components are weak equivalences induces a weak equivalence $\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}X_\alpha\to\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}Y_\alpha$; both colimits are cofibrant. No properness hypothesis on $\mathcal M$ is imposed.
